edit.description: `readQueueOnDisk` proves the queue's absence by descent from a root its caller answers for, instead of from the listing's errno
`EntryClaimStore.readHolders` the same, descending from the git common dir it already resolved
the queue reader's caller supplies the root it already holds
the queue reader's call sites here follow its signature

summary: The queue listing and the claim listing each key absence off ENOENT, so on win32 an obstructed directory dispatches a tick over an empty queue and reports nothing in flight

per.section: The fix lands at the mechanism

acceptance: the two listings whose absence verdict decides dispatch prove that absence by the same descent their sibling stores run, so an obstructed directory refuses by name on every host rather than reading as empty on one
tests: reading the pending queue under a path obstructed by a plain file refuses naming the queue
reading a repository's entry claims under an obstructed path refuses naming the claim store
notes: Verified this tick: `readQueueOnDisk` (`src/pendingLedger.ts:206`) and `readHolders` (`src/entryClaims.ts:111`) take the empty answer on ENOENT while their own docs (`:190`, `:95`) promise a refusal. On win32 an obstructed ancestor is ENOENT (`platform-facts.md`), so phases dispatch over no queue and the gate's claim check passes over an entry a build tick holds. Three siblings already descend: `src/mergingMarkers.ts:84`, `src/priorAttempts.ts:444`, `harness/dirListing.ts:88`.
